definitions.gloss: to cause trouble; to make waves; to stir things up
definitions.explanation: To disturb a peaceful situation by creating conflict or controversy. Literally 'to raise waves and wind.' Often used in the negative to advise against creating unnecessary conflict.

examples.japanese: {波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てたく⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: I don't want to make waves.

examples.japanese: ⟦あまり→あまり：00604_amari⟧{波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てない⟦ほうがいい→ほうがいい：10078_hougaii⟧。
examples.english: It's better not to stir things up too much.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一言|ひとこと}→一言：03708_hitokoto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{職場|しょくば}→職場：04164_shokuba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てることになった。
examples.english: His single remark ended up causing trouble at the workplace.

notes:
USAGE:
Very commonly used in the negative form ({波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てない) to express the desire to avoid conflict. Reflects the Japanese cultural value of maintaining harmony ({和|わ}). The related expression ⟦{波風|なみかぜ}→波風：16755_namikaze⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧ describes the intransitive version — trouble arising on its own.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てない (to not make waves)
- ⟦{波風|なみかぜ}→波風：16755_namikaze⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧ (waves arise; trouble brews)
- ⟦{波風|なみかぜ}→波風：16755_namikaze⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{立|た}たない→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧ (a peaceful life without trouble)
